master.headline: YES — robot is clearly improving — moderate signal of improvement across 199,990 packages over 152.6h of stream (2529 readings).
paragraphs: Overall throughput sits at 1,311 pach/h across 152.6h of stream (199,990 packages cumulative). Comparing the first 6.0h to the last 6.0h, the rate moved from 1,380 to 2,867 pach/h (+107.7%).
In the 8.8h split-challenge shift, the human won by 1.4% (robot 12,747 pkgs at 1,289 pach/h vs human 12,926 pkgs).

Per-OCR-pair rates are highly variable (CV 707.3% across 2503 samples, mean 1,527 pach/h). Time-of-day pattern shows a 404.9% spread between best UTC hour 1 (6,011 pach/h) and worst UTC hour 8 (1,190 pach/h).
What we know with confidence: the peak sustained rate is 1,500 pach/h at stream hour 38.0; current active robot is BOB (F.03); the solo_active phase carries the densest sample at 1,311 pach/h.
Worth watching next: whether the 404.9% time-of-day spread persists or flattens.
what_we_know: 199,990 packages sorted over 152.6h of stream → overall rate 1,311 pach/h.
Peak sustained rate: 1,500 pach/h at stream hour 38.0 (window 2.0h).
OCR-rate distribution: mean 1,527 pach/h, CV 707.3% → highly variable (2503 samples).
Shift record: 8.8h challenge, human won by 1.4% (robot 12,747 vs human 12,926).
Time-of-day spread: 404.9% between best UTC hour 1 and worst UTC hour 8.
what_we_dont_know: Source quality is mixed in the early stream: journalist estimates and historical OCR are blended with no robot identity, so comparisons to that period are biased.
Robot-vs-human performance generalises from a single shift record — one sample, no error bars.
Why the time-of-day spread is 404.9% — we observe the pattern but cannot yet attribute it (lighting? shift rotation? sample bias?).
watch_next: Continued OCR capture to keep the verdict confidence above 0.7.
